findings.title: Public findMany method removed with no caller updates in this PR
findings.body: This PR deletes the `findMany` method from `InsightsBookingService` (it previously ran `prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany` with the auth/filter conditions merged into the `where` clause) and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. No callers are updated in this PR. Any existing code that constructs `InsightsBookingService` and calls `findMany({ select, ... })` will fail to compile (or fail at runtime in untyped usage), and every caller now has to write its own `$queryRaw` with select/pagination/ordering logic, moving query construction out of the service. Before merging, verify there are zero callers of `findMany` (and of the old constructor option type) across the repo, or update them in this PR.

The PR description explicitly states the tests were never executed ('I encountered test runner configuration issues, so please verify the tests actually pass'). This PR rewrites the authorization logic of an insights service from Prisma where-inputs to hand-built raw SQL fragments (the highest-risk kind of change: security scoping for user/team/org data), and every assertion in this file was changed, yet none of them have been run. Notably, the new assertions compare `Prisma.Sql` objects with `toEqual`, which depends on Prisma's internal representation (own `_strings`/`values` properties), and the final test queries the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` table, whose population path for bookings created directly via `prisma.booking.create` is unverified. The tests must be executed and confirmed passing before merge rather than delegating verification to the human reviewer checklist.

findings.title: Order-dependent assertion on user ID arrays built from unordered membership queries
findings.body: The org-scope test asserts the exact `Prisma.sql` fragment including `"userId" = ANY(${[testData.user.id, user2.id, user3.id]})`. The service builds this array from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds` results deduplicated with `Array.from(new Set(...))`, which preserves whatever order the database returns rows in. If the repository query has no deterministic `ORDER BY`, the resulting array order is not guaranteed, and since `toEqual` on the `Prisma.Sql` values array is order-sensitive, this test can flake. The assertion should compare the ID set order-independently (or the service should sort the IDs).

findings.title: Caching tests deleted instead of converted
findings.body: The previous test file had a 'Caching' describe block verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` return cached results on second call. Those tests were removed rather than updated to the new `Prisma.Sql` return types, even though the caching logic (`cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` with `=== undefined` checks, including the subtle null-vs-undefined distinction for filter conditions) still exists in the service. This leaves a regression-prone behavior (e.g., breaking the null cache by using a falsy check) untested.
